instances.claim: This tells me that Chang chose the cent because of its art-historical standing — because Brenner's Lincoln is the most reproduced artwork on Earth.
instances.why: Line 3 is framed as an account of the choice ('the readymade he chose'), so the bare superlative in line 4 is read as a second item in that same account rather than as an independent fact. Nothing in the draft says the artwork's reproduction record played any part in the selection — line 1 locates the origin in a value discrepancy instead — yet the adjacency supplies an art-historical motive, converting a property of the object into a reason for picking it.

instances.claim: This tells me that the marks of touch and time on the objects are a product of the process Chang initiated.
instances.why: Placing the wear immediately after 'Chang initiated an ongoing process of redefinition' makes the marks read as that process's output, when a circulated cent's handling and age largely precede the work entirely. The order assigns the artist authorship of a pre-existing physical history that neither line claims for him.
